summary: Replaced mutable task references and save-on-exit behavior with immutable versioned values, complete edit/reopen/search workflows, explicit deletion confirmation and save-before-memory candidate commits.

Added strict bounded legacy/versioned decoding, completion invariants, stable ID watermarks, preserved original legacy backups, flushed atomic replacement and cooperative cross-process stale-file protection.
Stopped malformed startup and incomplete EOF from replacing existing data, and added explicit reload recovery after rejected stale writes.
Added 43 passing Java/process checks, preserved historical onboarding material and nine detailed learning documents connecting the CLI to future versioned CRUD HTTP and SQL design.

checks.environment: JDK 17; Python 3.13; disposable files; independent JVM concurrency
checks.command: python scripts/verify.py (35 Java tests, 8 CLI/process checks, UTF-8 compilation)

limits: The project remains a Java CLI; no HTTP/browser app, authentication, ownership, audit history or SQL deployment was added. The course explicitly identifies those extensions.
File locking is cooperative and atomic replacement depends on filesystem support; no power-loss, directory-flush, network-filesystem or multi-machine certification.
Rejected terminal input is not retained as a draft or automatically merged. Reload and deliberate re-entry are required after stale-file conflicts.
Strict legacy conversion preserves original bytes but does not repair arbitrary malformed records; snapshots are bounded to 8 MiB and 10,000 tasks.
